tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format, ensuring it is the last parseable list in the response.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the solution is ready to be submitted to the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing only a textual explanation without the move list, or placing the move list before other text so the parser misses it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that sit above it to other pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a required move involves a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 4 remains on top of it, leading to an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, resulting in a source‑top mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the placement is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which is smaller.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When you need to move a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg as auxiliary, recursively move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary, move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a full stack of consecutive disks resides on a single peg and must be transferred to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a stack of three disks without using the recursive pattern, leading to missing or out‑of‑order moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final arrangement, move those smaller disks elsewhere before placing the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg that still has disk 2 on top, which would place a larger disk on a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk that can legally be placed onto the goal peg before handling smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During planning for a final‑peg goal, prioritize moving the biggest movable disk to the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the goal peg before disk 5, causing the final order to be incorrect.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal; adjust if it does not.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full sequence of moves, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves disk 3 on a different peg than required, because the final state was never checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Treat the smallest disk (disk 1) as a universal temporary buffer: move it onto any larger disk or empty peg to free up space for moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary spot to hold a peg clear for moving a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Getting stuck because the smallest disk was never moved to create a free peg, preventing larger disks from being relocated.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid unnecessary back-and-forth moves; keep solution concise
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When planning the move sequence, each move should bring a disk closer to its final position; avoid moving a disk to a peg only to move it back later without progress.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the construction of the move list, to reduce move count and avoid wasted steps.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 from peg 0 to peg 1 and immediately back to peg 0, adding redundant moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model finishes without generating any moves, often because it stops after reasoning or forgets to output the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always produce at least one move; ensure the final answer contains a non‑empty move list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens before finishing the move list, leaving it incomplete.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan a concise solution, or break the move list into a single line that fits within the token budget.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is buried under smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not verify the size relationship between the moving disk and the destination peg's top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
